rule: No count padding. Every hypothesis must be discriminated against a simpler baseline and retain negative results.

hypotheses.claim: Sparse change-driven PerceptualField updates reduce compute/state movement versus full per-frame re-analysis on mostly static streams without material task loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched streams show <15% resource gain, worse p95, or >2 pp accuracy/calibration loss.

hypotheses.claim: Hybrid anchor-frame plus change-delta processing is Pareto-superior to fixed periodic full-frame processing for persistent FRANK workloads.
hypotheses.falsifier: A fixed periodic policy is Pareto-equal or better across representative held-out streams.

hypotheses.claim: Pure event/change-only processing is insufficient for static/slow semantic attributes and recovery after state loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Event-only preserves and reconstructs all required semantics with no anchor advantage.

hypotheses.claim: Adaptive anchor frequency driven by uncertainty, state age, action and recovery beats fixed anchor frequency.
hypotheses.falsifier: Best fixed period matches or beats adaptive policy on compute, stale-state error and recognition.

hypotheses.claim: Multi-timescale scheduling reduces redundant semantic inference relative to one synchronous vision loop.
hypotheses.falsifier: No material resource gain or ordering/replay failures outweigh benefits.

hypotheses.claim: Binding source timestamp/epoch before semantic transformation is necessary for robust stale/reorder handling.
hypotheses.falsifier: Late binding is equally safe under adversarial reorder, retry and replay.

hypotheses.claim: Post-action visual refresh has higher information/causal value than periodic refresh at equal visual-compute budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Periodic/random refresh matches outcome-detection latency and action attribution.

hypotheses.claim: Typed-state habituation suppresses repetitive visual/OCR work while preserving rare meaningful changes better than raw-similarity habituation.
hypotheses.falsifier: It hides meaningful changes or produces no load reduction.

hypotheses.claim: Bounded recurrence between sensor evidence and world/scene hypotheses improves occluded and ambiguous recognition over matched feedforward inference.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched feedforward reaches equivalent accuracy/calibration/cost or recurrence gain fails lesion/rescue.

hypotheses.claim: World-model priors help safely only when weighted by explicit bottom-up evidence precision.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fixed/unbounded priors are equally calibrated on misleading-prior and no-signal controls.

hypotheses.claim: Separating sensor evidence, learned/world prior and goal/context bias is necessary for auditable perceptual uncertainty.
hypotheses.falsifier: A fused score preserves equivalent calibration, diagnostics and counterfactual control with lower complexity.

hypotheses.claim: Prediction error should be typed by identity/spatial/temporal/attribute/provenance class rather than represented only as one scalar.
hypotheses.falsifier: Typed decomposition adds cost without improving routing, intervention choice or error localization.

hypotheses.claim: Set-valued perceptual alternatives reduce confidently wrong early commitment on ambiguous input.
hypotheses.falsifier: Top-1 early commitment is equally calibrated/accurate or alternative state causes prohibitive cost.

hypotheses.claim: Strong contradictory sensor evidence should reopen previously stabilized percepts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reopening adds instability without correcting more false beliefs than a non-reopening baseline.

hypotheses.claim: World/memory feedback is more valuable for relations, identity and occlusion than for high-SNR low-level attributes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Lesion gains are uniform, absent or confined to simple attributes.

hypotheses.claim: Goal context should control compute/attention but must not increase sensor-truth confidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Useful task focus requires contaminating evidential confidence or misses critical unexpected evidence.

hypotheses.claim: A prior-dominance readout predicts expectation-driven false percepts better than ordinary confidence alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: It has no incremental predictive value on misleading-prior/OOD tests.

hypotheses.claim: Adaptive recurrence stopping based on convergence/decision value beats a fixed iteration count.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fixed iterations are Pareto-superior on accuracy, latency and stability.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent object identity improves robustness to detector flicker and temporary occlusion.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stateless detection plus simple smoothing matches recall, relation stability and false-positive rate.

hypotheses.claim: OCCLUDED, ABSENT, OUT_OF_FOV, UNKNOWN and STALE require distinct states for correct temporal reasoning.
hypotheses.falsifier: Conflating them produces equivalent replay and downstream action outcomes.

hypotheses.claim: Explicit negative evidence should decay object visibility belief faster than mere non-observation.
hypotheses.falsifier: One universal decay rule is equally accurate on occlusion/disappearance sequences.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent entity identity must be independent of semantic label identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Label-derived identity is equally robust under misclassification and later refinement.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent spatial/relation hypotheses in ClayGraph reduce repeated compositional reconstruction at the 4B boundary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Per-frame reconstruction is equal/better in token cost and task performance.

hypotheses.claim: New visual relations should remain reversible/provisional until sufficient evidence supports stable world integration.
hypotheses.falsifier: Immediate stable writes have equal contamination and rollback behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Temporally linked region features improve fine-grained identity over repeated independent whole-image classification.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent classification matches identity continuity without extra false merges.

hypotheses.claim: Object and scene hypotheses should constrain each other bidirectionally while retaining separate provenance.
hypotheses.falsifier: One-direction or fully fused inference is equally accurate/calibrated and simpler.

hypotheses.claim: Sparse typed visual state deltas are a better canonical hot-path representation than repeated natural-language captions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Captions are equally compact, replayable and effective for downstream tasks.

hypotheses.claim: Evidence, perceptual hypothesis and persistent world entity require distinct logical identities.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unified nodes preserve all authority, uncertainty and counterfactual invariants with lower complexity.

hypotheses.claim: VisualPercept snapshots can be materialized on demand from evidence/state lineage instead of eagerly stored on every update.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reconstruction is unreliable, semantically divergent or more expensive overall.

hypotheses.claim: Some visual relations require n-ary/role-bound representation because pairwise edges lose binding semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Best pairwise/state-machine reduction is information-equivalent under interventions and cheaper.

hypotheses.claim: Retina ambiguity should reuse Hyperposition set-valued semantics rather than create a separate alternative-state system.
hypotheses.falsifier: Generic Hyperposition cannot express visual evidence/roles efficiently or clearly.

hypotheses.claim: Sensor recognition must never inherit execution authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any visual classification can mint effect capability without the external authority gateway; that is an architecture failure.

hypotheses.claim: Visual semantic identity can remain stable across physical encoder/detector lowerings when observations are semantically equivalent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Encoder swaps necessarily change canonical meaning despite matched evidence.

hypotheses.claim: Transform/model lineage enables selective invalidation of derived visual state after model/version/calibration changes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Only coarse global invalidation is reliable or selective invalidation misses dependencies.

hypotheses.claim: Most visual updates should remain below GWT; only unresolved/high-value states need global broadcast.
hypotheses.falsifier: Selective gating misses important events or saves negligible model/workspace cost.

hypotheses.claim: A typed vector of surprise, uncertainty, goal relevance, risk, conflict and action consequence selects visual GWT candidates better than one salience score.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single scalar is equally predictive/causally useful and simpler.

hypotheses.claim: GWT should receive the minimal causally relevant visual Assembly rather than the full PerceptualField.
hypotheses.falsifier: Bounded projection loses material task performance or full-field context cost is negligible.

hypotheses.claim: Expected information gain from an additional sensing action should enter visual candidate value.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fixed cascade or random second-look policy resolves ambiguity equally well at lower/equal cost.

hypotheses.claim: Active sensing should stop when expected information/task value falls below compute/latency/risk cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fixed sensing budgets are more robust on held-out tasks.

hypotheses.claim: Post-action visual re-entry is necessary for visually grounded effect-outcome verification.
hypotheses.falsifier: Nonvisual receipts alone provide equivalent causal closure on tested visual tasks.

hypotheses.claim: Visual GWT episodes require separate delivery, reconstruction, uptake, causal-use, outcome and re-entry receipts.
hypotheses.falsifier: These stages empirically collapse without losing causal diagnosis.

hypotheses.claim: Cross-modal conflict is a high-value GWT trigger even when each modality alone has moderate confidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Conflict gating produces false alarms without improving consistency/outcomes.

hypotheses.claim: The fixed 80-class YOLOv8n detector is a major source of long-tail hard-set failure and should be benchmarked against open-vocabulary/open-world detection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Alternatives fail to improve held-out utility after latency/RAM/calibration costs.

hypotheses.claim: MobileCLIP2 can improve the edge accuracy-latency-memory frontier relative to current CLIP-B/32 on at least one FRANK target device.
hypotheses.falsifier: CLIP-B/32 remains Pareto-superior on project x86/Android workloads.

hypotheses.claim: SigLIP2 dense/localization features can replace some separate scene/region heuristics with better localized semantic evidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: No held-out binding/localization gain survives runtime cost.

hypotheses.claim: Small/distilled DINOv3 candidates may improve temporal region correspondence over current DINOv2.
hypotheses.falsifier: DINOv2 is equal/better on tracking, relation stability and runtime.

hypotheses.claim: Free-form captioning should be conditional rather than always-on because it can amplify wrong detector priors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Always-on captioning provides higher calibrated marginal utility per cost with no extra error cascades.

hypotheses.claim: Hand-written narrative aggregation should leave the canonical hot truth path and become a projection over typed state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Typed-state cognition underperforms narrative-state cognition enough to justify canonical narrative coupling.

hypotheses.claim: The Game-of-Life feature stage has value only if it adds held-out information beyond cheap texture/dense-feature baselines after compute control.
hypotheses.falsifier: Its incremental value disappears; then it is removed/demoted.

hypotheses.claim: In-process sensor/perception integration lowers IPC/serialization latency relative to standalone Retina service on project hardware.
hypotheses.falsifier: Process isolation is equal/faster or its safety/recovery benefit dominates measured latency gain.

hypotheses.claim: Open-set UNKNOWN detection is more important to FRANK safety than maximizing closed-set top-1 coverage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Closed-set confidence is already reliably calibrated on unseen/adversarial objects and action outcomes.

hypotheses.claim: Historical CLIP-lenient threshold 0.20 is too permissive for truth claims.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent frozen realistic-negative calibration shows acceptable FPR and downstream risk at 0.20.

hypotheses.claim: Freezing held-out images/vocabulary before tuning will reveal lower generalization than the post-gap-close hard-set score.
hypotheses.falsifier: Clean held-out performance remains statistically comparable.

hypotheses.claim: YOLO, CLIP, OCR and other component scores need explicit calibration before fusion because their raw confidences are not commensurate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Raw-score fusion is equally calibrated/reliable across conditions.

hypotheses.claim: Lineage-aware dependency invalidation prevents one wrong upstream detection from cascading into persistent false facts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent downstream stages self-correct equally well without dependency tracking.

hypotheses.claim: Perceptual state must be crash/restart replay-compatible to avoid silent divergence from sensor history.
hypotheses.falsifier: Arbitrary crash injection produces equivalent state without dedicated replay/checkpoint semantics.

hypotheses.claim: Source/epoch lineage is necessary to reject stale/replayed visual inputs before they mutate live world state.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler mechanism blocks all stale/replay mutations equivalently.

hypotheses.claim: OCR/visual text must remain observed content and never instruction authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any visual-text-only path can alter effect authority; that is a safety failure, not support.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent visual state can make a text/Clay-native 4B functionally multimodal without native image tokens.
hypotheses.falsifier: The 4B cannot exploit structured visual state sufficiently on required multimodal tasks.

hypotheses.claim: PerceptualField Assembly projections use fewer model tokens than caption/full-JSON projections on persistent scenes at matched task quality.
hypotheses.falsifier: No token reduction or material task loss occurs.

hypotheses.claim: The principal gain of dissolved perception is persistent state reuse rather than superior isolated single-image recognition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Long-horizon gain is absent or single-image gain dominates.

hypotheses.claim: A 4B trained to read typed Clay visual state will be more efficient/robust than one reading verbose Retina narratives.
hypotheses.falsifier: Narrative inputs remain equal/better on held-out tasks and token cost.

hypotheses.claim: Typed active-sensing requests are safer/more reproducible than free-form vision requests from the 4B.
hypotheses.falsifier: Free-form requests are equally deterministic, cost-aware and provenance-safe.

hypotheses.claim: Perceptual/world state can continue updating while the LLM is idle, improving grounding at the next model call.
hypotheses.falsifier: Asynchronous state causes more drift than continuity benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Selective visual projection makes model-visible context grow sublinearly with stream duration.
hypotheses.falsifier: Visual context still grows approximately with frame count or required detail is lost.

hypotheses.claim: The correct claim is system-level functional multimodality, not literal conversion of the underlying text model into a native VLM.
hypotheses.falsifier: Scope changes only if the future target model itself receives/trains native visual tokens.

counterhypotheses.claim: Optimized feedforward Retina plus temporal caching can match recurrent-field gains at lower complexity.
A separate Retina process is superior because fault isolation/deployment scheduling outweigh IPC overhead.
Recurrence gains mostly exploit dataset regularities rather than genuine perceptual completion.
A native VLM remains necessary for required compositional/spatial/long-tail semantics.
Persistent object state creates more harmful ghosts/stale beliefs than detector flicker it fixes.
Event/change scheduling is too complex and fixed low-rate full frames are safer overall.
Typed Clay visual state is less usable by the 4B than concise natural-language captions without expensive retraining.
GWT gating saves little because expensive perception kernels must run before salience is known.
Active sensing adds more latency/complexity than useful information for target desktop/screen workloads.
Open-vocabulary/open-world detectors are too slow, heavy or poorly calibrated for target CPU/Android hardware.
MobileCLIP2/SigLIP2/DINOv3 benchmark gains do not transfer to Retina workloads/hardware.
The historical GoL stage contains unique cheap texture cues and should remain.
Evidence/hypothesis/world planes are overengineering; one immutable event log plus derived views is sufficient.
Set-valued ambiguity causes state explosion; calibrated top-k plus abstention is enough.
One-module physical fusion enlarges crash radius enough to erase latency advantages.
Long-horizon visual memory should live in a dedicated streaming-video memory system rather than ClayGraph/UDB.
Priors belong only in high-level reasoning; early visual recurrence is too contamination-prone.
Clay serialization/training overhead erases token savings of structured visual state.
A simple tracker plus periodic detector captures nearly all useful temporal continuity.
Clean held-out phrase coverage remains a sufficient engineering proxy for downstream LLM usefulness when paired with calibration metrics.
